title: Assess packed CLI completeness
description: Assess the actual emitted CLI package and its clean-consumer behavior against the existing package policy. It supplies attributable qualification observations rather than accepting source configuration as proof of the packed product.
inputs: Actual CLI tarball, declared runtime inclusion/exclusion policy, and bundled trust metadata.
Selected real target archives and prepared clean-consumer assessment conditions.
outputs: Packed-member, executable, dependency/hook, metadata, and installed-consumer observations.
Missing, forbidden, unsafe, unperformed, or incomplete package qualification findings.
behavior: Inspect actual members, executable entrypoint, public/license metadata, required runtime files, and bundled trust inputs.
Reject forbidden contents, secrets, missing runtime dependencies, unjustified hooks, or consumer generation/hidden acquisition.
Exercise the actual packed binary in a clean consumer context without repository-only imports.
Assess producer-to-packed-installer composition for the selected targets and required conflict, replacement, preservation, and safety partitions.
Return observed scope and remaining gaps for general evidence retention and release qualification.

failure_behavior.condition: A required runtime input is absent or a forbidden member or hook is present.
failure_behavior.outcome: Report the package defect and prevent qualification.

failure_behavior.condition: Only a source checkout, mocked pass, helper, or dry-run is available.
failure_behavior.outcome: Report the unassessed packed-consumer boundary rather than claiming composed product proof.

failure_behavior.condition: An actual candidate check cannot complete.
failure_behavior.outcome: Retain obtained observations and identify the incomplete scope.

sources.basis: Logical behavior derived from the identified published-product contracts for IR-010; existing source details and compatibility/adoption limits remain applicable.
